newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Italians in Chechnya may be freed soon - Russia.
newsitem.headline: Italians in Chechnya may be freed soon - Russia.

text.p: Three Italian aid workers who went missing in Chechnya on September 26 could be freed very soon, Itar-Tass news agency quoted a senior Russian military commander as saying on Saturday.

Vyacheslav Obchinnikov, who leads the Russian element of the joint police command in the capital Grozny, told the agency he had been assured by a Chechen separatist security official that the Italians "will be returned no later than today".
The agency the Italians worked for, InterSOS, said last week it suspected they had been kidnapped.

Sandro Pocaterra, 41, and two doctors, Augusto Lombardo, 36, and Giuseppe Valenti, 62, were last seen as they set off by car from Nazran for Grozny, about 100 km (60 miles) away to deliver medicine and equipment.
Kidnappings are common in the chaos of the Chechen conflict. In many cases, foreigners have been seized by bandits looking to steal money or be paid ransom.
